messages.subject: Re: CIM & Epistatic mapping
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dong,

You have those pretty much right, though argmax.geno() doesn't simulate
the genotypes, but rather calculates the most probable sequence of
underlying
genotypes given the available marker data.

It's possible to export inferred genotypes for use in other software;
likely
fill.geno() is the only one that would be useful for that.  If your
dataset
is called "mycross", then the following imputes the missing or partially
informative (or possibly in error) genotypes and copies them over the
observed data:

   mycross <- fill.geno(mycross)

You can then use write.cross() to write the data back to a file.
There are
mapmaker ("mm") and QTL Cartographer formats ("qtlcart").  I've not
tested
this function all that much.

If your genotype data, consisting mostly of dominant markers, are not
very
informative (try looking at plot.info <http://plot.info>(mycross) to see how much
information
is missing), you could be severely misled by the above approach, as
you'd be
inferring the underlying truth, and then pretending that those
inferred genotypes
were precisely the truth.  Important uncertainty would not be taken
into account.
I think your best bet is to stick with analysis via scanone(), scantwo
(),
or fitqtl(), using either EM or imputation to take account of that
uncertainty.

karl

messages.body_plain:
I seem to have a problem with the read.cross command in R/qtl removing
SNP genotype data on the X chromosome that it doesn't like.  The
removed genotypes appear to possibly be the result of
double-recombination events in both gametes (ie: F2 intercross female X
chromosome genotypes: B A A A A A A A A A A B B B B B, where B=BB,
A=AA, and H=AB or BA).  This also happens in the F3 progeny from the
same cross if there are apparent double-recombination events in one or
both gametes (ie: F3 intercross female X chromosome genotypes: B B B A
A H H H H H H H H H H H).  Am I simply setting up the pgm column wrong
on the data, or is there some other explanation for the data removal?
Is there a way to prevent R/qtl from removing this data?

Thanks,
Gloria

messages.subject: Re: read.cross removing genotype data
messages.body_plain:
Dear Gloria,

In your F2 data, there is one individual indicated to be a female but
having
genotype data that indicates a male (only A's and B's).  Reading in the
data, I get the warning message "Omitting 10 AA genotypes from females
from cross (BxA)x(BxA) on the X chr."  Those are all from that one
individual.
It drops those A genotypes, but probably it's better to check the sex
of the
individual and either fix that or drop the individual.

Unfortunately, your F3 data is problematic for R/qtl.  We don't
really have
facilities for analyzing genotype data from an F2.  The autosomal
data might
be treated as an F2 with an expanded map, but the X chromosome data
doesn't
fit our scheme.  We're just not set up to deal with an F3.

Regards,
karl

first question is what is the best QTL model to use to analyze thesee

messages.subject: Re: Summary.scantwo
messages.body_plain:
summary.scantwo picks out just a single point from each chromosome pair
(just as summary.scanone picks out just a single point from each
chromosome).

If you want to look at further details, you need to study the
contents of
the out.two object itself.  out.two$lod is a matrix with all of the
LOD scores.

karl

I think, I have figured out the issue. The problem was that I had been
using symbols PP, PB, BB to mark the genotype combinations. The program
seems not to have liked this, since after I did the following change in
the csv data file before loading into workspace:

PB->AB ... (PWD/B6 allelic combination) on autosomes
BB->AA ... (B6/B6 allelic combination) on autosomes
PP->BB ... (B6/Y allelic combination) on X
BB->AA  ... (PWD/Y allelic combination) on X

and added the "sex" column, the program loaded all data smoothly as a
backcross:

> HstQTL5 <- read.cross("csv", dir="/Users/Radek/Documents/Protocols/2006_05/0605HstQTL/",file="HstQTLbbedit5.csv",genotypes=c("AA","AB","BB", "not PP","not BB"),convertXdata=T)

 --Read the following data:
	 53  individuals
	 119  markers
	 3  phenotypes
